visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The video opens with a close-up of a soft, cream-colored Nike fleece jacket hanging on a white plastic hanger. The creator's hand with manicured nails holds the Marshalls price tag, which clearly displays a price of $16.99. In the background, out-of-focus clothing racks filled with various garments are visible under bright, even department store lighting. (2) A hand holds a printed receipt from Marshalls alongside a pink five-dollar bill. The receipt details various purchases like 'INF & TODDLERS' items and shows a subtotal of $192.95. The background is a slightly blurred view of a retail checkout area with wooden surfaces and shopping bags. (3) The scene shifts to an outdoor view of a classic New York building facade at 620 6th Avenue. Scaffolding covers the lower levels, where signs for Marshalls and T.J. Maxx are prominently displayed. A yellow New York City taxi and a person on a bicycle pass by on the wet asphalt street under daylight. (4) Inside the store, the camera captures an escalator descending into a large retail space. A bright red T.J. Maxx sign is visible in the background next to a decorated Christmas tree. People are seen riding the escalator or walking through the aisles, creating a busy shopping atmosphere. (5) A hand gestures towards shelves stocked with boxed goods, including UGG-branded white boxes and designer handbags from Michael Kors, Calvin Klein, and DKNY. The lighting is sharp and clinical, typical of a large department store, highlighting the organized display of accessories and footwear. (6) The creator explores the shoe section, showing long rows of shoe boxes on metal shelves. Close-ups feature pink and white Nike sneakers, fluffy brown slippers with a Marshalls tag showing $24.99, black Hunter boots priced at $59.99, and Minnetonka moccasins. The camera moves quickly between items to show variety. (7) A wide shot shows a man looking at a smartphone while sitting on a bench in the shoe department. The camera then pans up to show overhead signs for 'Girls' and 'Baby' clothing sections. The store layout is dense with merchandise, using white pillars and fluorescent ceiling lights. (8) The focus moves to children's clothing, displaying a grey Champion hoodie and a white Nike sweatshirt. Price overlays in Taiwanese Dollars (NT$400, NT$500) appear on screen to provide context for viewers. The hands-on presentation shows the texture of the fabric and the tags attached to the hangers. (9) At the checkout counter, the creator sorts through a large pile of purchased clothes, including jackets and pants. A final close-up of the receipt shows a total of $192.95 and a payment of $200.00. The lighting remains bright, and the interaction with the cashier's station is visible. (10) The video concludes with the creator walking out of the store into an entrance hall. She is dressed in a long tan coat, a white knitted beanie, and fluffy slippers, carrying two oversized Marshalls paper shopping bags. A small inset image of a smiling baby appears briefly, followed by a final shot of her waving in front of the escalator.

audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) A female narrator begins speaking in a very enthusiastic and high-pitched voice. The speech rate is fast and energetic, matching the upbeat, high-tempo pop/electronic BGM which features a driving 4/4 beat and bright synthesizer pads. A distinct bubble-pop sound effect accompanies the appearance of the first on-screen text. (2) As the narrator describes the low prices of the Nike jacket, her vocal arousal remains high with frequent upward inflections. The BGM continues steadily at around 120 BPM. Very faint rustling sounds of paper or fabric are audible under the voice, suggesting a field recording environment within the store. (3) The acoustic texture shifts briefly as the scene moves outdoors. Although the BGM and voice dominate, a subtle low-frequency hum of city traffic is present. The narrator's tone becomes more informational as she introduces the location. A soft whoosh SFX transitions the audio back to the indoor store environment. (4) During the shoe section montage, the narrator uses a rhythmic delivery, timing her words to the beat of the music. Multiple ding bell-like sound effects are used as musical accents whenever a new price tag is shown. The background noise of the store crowd murmur is very low. (5) In the final phase, the narrator's voice takes on a warm and satisfied tone while she talks about her large haul. The BGM remains energetic until the last few seconds, where it begins a gradual fade. The overall mix is clean with a high signal-to-noise ratio, prioritizing vocal clarity over environmental sounds.
